To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) there is a linear relation between surface brightness and size of globular clusters, (ii) this is not a primordial relation at cluster formation, (iii) the scatter around this scaling law is approximately 1 mag in surface brightness, and (iv) the slope of the fundamental line is approximately -1.5.

(1) the fundamental line scaling relation holds for a large sample of Galactic and extragalctic clusters, (2) the scatter in SBe is approximately 1 mag and (3) the scatter is larger for clusters that are younger than the half-light relaxation time and decreases with cluster age.

(1) there is a linear relation between the surface brightness and effective radius of globular clusters, (2) this relation has a scatter of 1m ag, and (3) this scatter decreases with increasing dynamical age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin and evolution of the fundamental line of globular clusters.
the fundamental line of globular clusters and its relation to stellar population evolution and dynamical evolution.
the fundamental line of Galactic and extragalctic globular clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fundamental line is the result of the interplay between two-body relaxation, stellar population evolution, and cluster age.
the fundamental plane of globular clusters is not a fundamental plane, but a fundamental line.
the fundamental plane of globular clusters is the result of stellar population evolution, and that this is modulated by dynamical processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fundamental line is a consequence of the dynamical evolution of globular clusters.
the fundamental line scaling relation is a consequence of two-body relaxation, which acts to reduce the scatter in SBe for clusters with longer half-light relaxation times.
the observed scaling laws of galactic and globular clusters are the consequence of the interplay between stellar evolution, dynamical evolution and the cluster initial mass function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while a scaling law does exist between SBe and Re, it is not as simple as it was previously thought.
the fundamental plane is a consequence of the evolution of the cluster stellar populations.
a purely photometrical relation exists between SBe and Re, and it is a powerful tool to estimate the size of globular clusters, even in the absence of detailed surface brightness profiles.
